marylandBudgetBill.citation: Md. Const. art. III, sec. 52(6b) (with sec. 52(6a) and (8)(d))
marylandBudgetBill.quote: In enacting a balanced Budget Bill as required under this Section for fiscal year 2024 and each fiscal year thereafter, the General Assembly may amend the bill by increasing, diminishing, or adding items therein relating to the General Assembly, by increasing, diminishing, or adding items therein relating to the judiciary, and by increasing, diminishing, or adding items therein relating to the Executive Department, provided that the total of the appropriation for the Executive Department approved by the General Assembly does not exceed the total proposed appropriation for the Executive Department submitted by the Governor. ... When passed by both Houses, the Budget Bill shall be a law immediately without further action by the Governor.
marylandBudgetBill.effect: The governor has no item veto (and no veto at all) over the Budget Bill: since fiscal year 2024, sec. 52(6b) makes the Budget Bill law immediately on passage by both houses, without further action by the governor. The governor's control comes before passage: the governor writes the Budget Bill, and the legislature may raise, cut or add Executive Department items only if its Executive Department total does not exceed the governor's. The older sec. 52(6a) regime, still printed in the text, let the legislature only strike or reduce items (except its own and the judiciary's) and then sent the bill to the governor under art. II, sec. 17. Supplementary Appropriation Bills, each limited to 'some single work, object or purpose', still go to the governor under art. II, sec. 17 (sec. 52(8)(a), (d)).
